title: Frontend: Notification Bell
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Notification Bell. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({items=[{id:a,text:Hello,read:false},{id:b,text:Update,read:false}]}). Bell[data-action=bell] toggles panel. Unread count [data-testid=unread] derives from records. Mark read[data-read=ID] is idempotent and disables itself. Opening must not mark messages read.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep notification identity and read state in records and derive unread count.
alternativeApproaches: Add server acknowledgements so delayed read updates cannot resurrect old unread states.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty panel; duplicate event; mark twice.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
